original_text: This model approximates the results obtained from the electromagnetic (EM) field simulation by \cite{Sun_2022}, as thoroughly validated in the work of \cite{Yusimu}.
injected_text: This model approximates the results obtained from the simulation by \cite{Sun_2022}, as thoroughly validated in the work of \cite{Yusimu}.
rationale: Drops the precise methodological qualifier 'electromagnetic (EM) field' from a citation to Sun_2022, whose central contribution (per its title 'The Electromagnetic Characteristics of the Tianlai Cylindrical Pathfinder Array') is specifically electromagnetic field simulation; the citing claim becomes generic 'simulation', which is less faithful to the cited paper's stated method.
ground_truth_description: Removed the methodological qualifier 'electromagnetic (EM) field' from the description of Sun_2022's simulation, leaving the cite key intact but weakening the methodological characterization.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: This model approximates the results obtained from the electromagnetic (EM) field simulation by \cite{Sun_2022}, as thoroughly validated in the work of \cite{Yusimu}.

original_text: we show the visibility for a short north-south baseline at 750 MHz.
injected_text: we show the visibility for a short north-south baseline at 570 MHz.
rationale: The abstract of this paper contains no numerical claim at all, so a strict 'abstract headline number' digit-swap is not realisable; the closest analog is the most prominent quoted result-figure caption sentence in the body. I swap the adjacent digits 7<->5 in '750 MHz' (the center frequency repeatedly stated as the TCPA's operating center, e.g. Sec. 2.3.1 'The center frequency of the TCPA is 750 MHz' and the Fig. 2 caption '(750 MHz)'). After the edit the same headline value is quoted both as 570 MHz (Sec. 3.3, describing the best-fit data_fit figure) and as 750 MHz (Sec. 2.3.1 and Fig. 2 caption), creating a same-paper internal inconsistency for the predicate, and crossing the band boundary (700-800 MHz) which makes it factually obviously wrong on a single read.
ground_truth_description: Adjacent-digit swap of the headline frequency at which the data-fit example is shown, changing '750 MHz' to '570 MHz' in Sec. 3.3 while the same value remains correctly quoted as '750 MHz' in Sec. 2.3.1 and the Fig. 2 caption.

truth.location_cue: we show the visibility for a short north-south baseline at 570 MHz
truth.paired_location: Sec. 2.3.1 (Baseline Selection): 'The center frequency of the TCPA is 750 MHz, corresponding to a wavelength lambda of 0.4 m'; also Fig. 2 caption '(750 MHz)'.
truth.quantity_label: TCPA observing center frequency (MHz) at which the data-fit example in Fig. fig:data_fit is shown

rationale: The displayed visibility equation is a load-bearing instance of the van Cittert--Zernike relation; replacing the canonical Fourier-kernel coefficient 2\pi/\lambda by \pi/\lambda produces a structurally similar but algebraically incorrect formula (factor-of-2 perturbation of a well-known physics-law coefficient), exactly the mechanism specified for mathematics S3 type 2.
ground_truth_description: In the calibrated visibility equation (eq2:calvis), the standard interferometric phase factor exp(-2\pi i (r_j-r_i)\cdot n / \lambda) was replaced by exp(-\pi i (r_j-r_i)\cdot n / \lambda), halving the canonical coefficient.

truth.term_role: Fourier-kernel phase coefficient (canonical 2\pi/\lambda in van Cittert--Zernike visibility relation)

original_text: The length of these baselines are all 3.2m.
injected_text: The length of these baselines are all 3.2m. The visibilities from all 12 baselines are then jointly combined into a single stacked likelihood, which suppresses per-baseline systematics and ensures that the recovered N-S beam parameters are consistent across the full set of selected baselines.
rationale: The inserted sentence asserts that all 12 selected N-S baselines are jointly combined in a stacked likelihood for the beam fit, but the Results section ('Measurement of the North-South Primary Beam') explicitly states that the fit uses visibilities from only three baselines (A1-A9, A2-A10, A4-A12), so a reviewer cross-checking Methods against Results sees a clear protocol inconsistency.
ground_truth_description: Added a sentence to the Methods (N-S beam) claiming a joint stacked-likelihood fit over all 12 selected baselines, contradicting the Results section which fits using only 3 baselines.
